hero.title: The open-source recruitment infrastructure for modern companies.
hero.description: OpenSya is an open-source infrastructure that enables companies to build, customize, and fully own their recruitment system.
hero.summary: A shared foundation. Installable modules. A platform designed to evolve with every organization.
hero.tagline: Modular, scalable, and fully owned by you.
hero.status: OpenSya is currently in an active design and development phase.

problem.title: Recruitment should not depend on rigid software
problem.subtitle: Every company hires differently. Why should their tools all work the same way?
problem.description: Recruitment processes vary based on a company’s size, organization, roles, regulatory constraints, and culture.
problem.introduction: Yet most software imposes its own way of working:
items: workflows that are difficult to customize;
data hosted in a system the company does not control;
little freedom to build for specific needs.
problem.conclusion: As the organization grows, its tool often becomes a constraint.
problem.quote: Companies should not have to adapt to their recruitment software. The software should adapt to the company.

positioning.title: More than an ATS
positioning.subtitle: OpenSya is not designed to be just another recruitment application.
positioning.description: An ATS provides a product with a predefined set of features. OpenSya aims to provide infrastructure.
positioning.definition: A technical and functional foundation on which a company, product team, or integrator can build its own recruitment environment.
items: install only the modules you need;
integrate OpenSya with your existing information system;
host the platform in the environment of your choice;
retain control over the code, data, and product evolution.
positioning.conclusion: OpenSya does not seek to impose a single way of recruiting. It provides the foundations that allow every organization to build its own.

principles.title: A platform you own
principles.subtitle: Your recruitment. Your processes. Your data. Your infrastructure.
principles.description: OpenSya is built on four core principles.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.description: The platform’s inner workings are visible, understandable, and open to improvement. Companies can audit the code, contribute to the project, or build their own extensions.

modular.title: Modular
modular.description: Each organization installs only the capabilities it needs. Modules can extend the backend, user interface, data models, workflows, integrations, and business rules.

selfHosted.title: Self-hosted
selfHosted.description: OpenSya is designed to run in the infrastructure chosen by the organization. Public cloud, private cloud, or internal infrastructure: the company remains in control of its environment.

extensible.title: Extensible
extensible.description: OpenSya must adapt to needs that do not exist yet. Its architecture makes it possible to compose modules, replace components, and build specialized experiences.

useCases.title: One foundation, many possibilities
useCases.subtitle: Build the recruitment system your organization actually needs.

internalPlatform.title: An internal recruitment platform
internalPlatform.description: Centralize job openings, applications, interviews, assessments, and collaboration between recruiters and hiring managers.

careerPortal.title: A career portal
careerPortal.description: Create a candidate experience aligned with your brand, roles, and recruitment strategy.

multisite.title: A multi-site recruitment system
multisite.description: Adapt processes to subsidiaries, teams, countries, or entities while maintaining shared governance.

specializedSolution.title: A specialized business solution
specializedSolution.description: Build a platform dedicated to a specific industry, hiring model, or organization.

commercialProduct.title: A commercial recruitment product
commercialProduct.description: Use OpenSya as the technical foundation for a solution designed for your own customers.

useCases.conclusion: The same infrastructure can support multiple products, interfaces, and operating models.

model.title: A stable Core. Composable capabilities. Freedom to evolve.
model.description: OpenSya is designed as an ecosystem made up of several complementary layers.

core.title: OpenSya Core
core.description: The Core provides the foundational capabilities shared by every recruitment platform:
core.conclusion: The Core is not intended to contain every possible feature. It provides a consistent foundation on which they can be built.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Modules add functional or technical capabilities without unnecessarily weighing down the foundation.
modules.conclusion: A module can provide interfaces, routes, services, business rules, data models, and configuration.

extensions.title: Company-specific extensions
extensions.description: When a need is specific, the organization can create its own modules. It does not have to wait for a vendor to add the capability to its roadmap.

architecture.title: An architecture built to last
architecture.subtitle: Needs change. The infrastructure must keep up.
architecture.description: OpenSya is built around a convention-driven full-stack architecture. The system discovers, connects, and orchestrates the different parts of the application so teams can focus on their business domain.
items: APIs and events designed for integration;
a clear separation between domain and infrastructure;
a design suited to modern deployments.
architecture.conclusion: The goal is not only to accelerate initial development. It is to make OpenSya platforms understandable, testable, and maintainable for years to come.

persistence.title: OpenSya Persistence
persistence.subtitle: The business domain before the database.
persistence.description: At the heart of a recruitment platform are complex rules: who can view or modify an application, which transitions are allowed, how an operation is validated, when automation is triggered, and how a reliable history is preserved.
persistence.definition: OpenSya Persistence is the engine responsible for consistently executing these rules around data.
persistence.adapterDescription: It operates above database adapters. The goal is to use PostgreSQL today, then support other environments such as MySQL, SQLite, or MongoDB without locking the OpenSya domain into a specific technology.
persistence.conclusion: OpenSya Persistence is designed first and foremost to power OpenSya, but its architecture also allows it to be used in other TypeScript applications.

audiences.title: Who are we building OpenSya for?
audiences.subtitle: Shared infrastructure for multiple stakeholders.

companies.title: For companies
companies.description: Organizations that want long-term control over their recruitment platform, data, and costs.

technicalTeams.title: For technical teams
technicalTeams.description: Developers who want to build a business solution without starting from scratch or depending on a closed product.

integrators.title: For integrators
integrators.description: Consultancies and service companies that want to deploy platforms tailored to their clients’ processes.

publishers.title: For software vendors
publishers.description: Product teams that want to create specialized recruitment software from an open-source foundation.

community.title: For the community
community.description: Contributors who believe essential business infrastructure can be open, shared, and built collectively.

philosophy.title: A different way to think about recruitment software
philosophy.subtitle: OpenSya does not replace one dependency with another.
philosophy.description: The project aims to build a different relationship between companies and their tools.

ownership.title: Ownership over permanent renting
ownership.description: An organization should be able to keep its system, its data, and its custom developments.

composition.title: Composition over accumulation
composition.description: Capabilities should be added as needed without turning the product into a monolithic platform.

interoperability.title: Interoperability over lock-in
interoperability.description: OpenSya must be able to communicate with the HR tools, internal systems, and external services already in use.

conventions.title: Conventions over repetitive complexity
conventions.description: The infrastructure automates predictable tasks while keeping business rules explicit.

community.title: Community over a closed roadmap
community.description: Needs are not determined by a software vendor alone. Companies, developers, and integrators can participate in the project’s evolution.

ambition.title: An ambition bigger than a product
ambition.subtitle: Building open infrastructure for the future of recruitment.
ambition.description: Our ambition is not simply to release an open-source ATS. We want to create a foundation capable of supporting a true ecosystem:
items: open standards for exchanging data and events;
a community that shares the same foundations without imposing the same products.
ambition.conclusion: Over time, OpenSya should enable multiple recruitment experiences to be built on shared infrastructure. Companies should not have to choose between a product that is quick to adopt and a system they truly control.

status.title: OpenSya is under construction.
status.description: The technical foundations and architectural principles are currently being designed, implemented, and stabilized.
status.warning: The project is not yet ready for production use.
items: defining the first functional use cases.
status.conclusion: This phase is intentionally open. It allows us to build the foundations with developers, recruitment professionals, pilot companies, and partners who share the project’s vision.

contribution.title: Help build OpenSya
contribution.subtitle: Great infrastructure is not built alone.
contribution.description: OpenSya is looking for people and organizations that want to take part in its early stages.

companies.title: Companies and HR teams
companies.description: Share your processes, constraints, and the limitations you encounter with your current tools.

developers.title: Developers
developers.description: Explore the architecture, start discussions, and contribute to the technical foundations.

designPartners.title: Design partners
designPartners.description: Help us test OpenSya against real-world use cases and define the first priority capabilities.

partners.title: Integrators and partners
partners.description: Help build an ecosystem of deployment, support, and extensions around the project.

closing.title: Your recruitment tool should belong to you.
closing.description: Your processes. Your integrations. Your business rules. Your ability to evolve.
closing.conclusion: OpenSya is building the open-source infrastructure that will enable companies to take back control of their recruitment.
closing.tagline: Modular, scalable, and fully owned by you.
closing.notice: OpenSya is an open-source project under active development. The documentation, APIs, and architecture are subject to change.

footer.description: The open-source recruitment infrastructure for modern companies.
